baseline.scope: Frozen desktop and current production UI at baseline; core, dependencies and fixture shared.

Actual Linux Electron main sleeps 6.5 seconds with Atomics.wait while its renderer types 12 revisions independently. saveDraft remains the real synchronous private-file implementation; override only counts calls. External parent samples OS process-tree memory while main cannot process IPC. No forced GC, debugger, providers or real physical-disk benchmark. All queued renderer changes and exit snapshot are checked in actual recovery files and reopened editors.

method: Three serial fresh desktop pairs per workload, middle pair order reversed. External parent requests procfs samples every 100 ms while actual main sleeps 6.5 seconds and renderer typing continues. No delayed/fake saveDraft implementation, debugger, forced GC, builds/tests or concurrent agent-run benchmarks. Every accepted sample has complete process-tree accounting; rejected attempts are preserved. All app main PIDs are absent after teardown. Sampled maxima are not continuous peaks or general speedup estimates.
scope: Deliberate event-loop stall, not measured physical-disk latency. Main cannot decode queued IPC during the stall; external OS sampling includes native transport/process pages. PSS apportions shared pages and excludes sampler/Xvfb/external services/driver memory outside descendants. GC is natural but not traced in this case. Actual final recovery and reopened text are exact; draft data already reached its writer before navigation. No installed Windows/macOS or general leak-free/bounded-app-memory claim.
